verdict: OK to lend in Gondal cotton ginning and pressing, but only to ginners with owned/controlled kapas sourcing, hedged or back-to-back lint sales and a tight 60-90 day cash cycle; avoid traders and job-work pressers with no gin of their own.
title: Gondal cotton ginning & pressing: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What the business physically is
A ginning and pressing unit buys seed cotton (kapas) at the Gondal APMC yard, separates lint from seed, bales and presses the lint, and sells to spinning mills; seed goes to oil mills. **Cash is made on the spread between kapas bought and lint sold, not on volume.** Gondal taluka has the highest cotton cultivation in Rajkot district and Gujarat ranks first in cotton production [1] — that is the local raw-material base, and it is the only city-specific fact we have. Sources say little else about Gondal itself, so the rest of this note is first principles plus peers. ## Where value and cash sit
Ginning is low value-adding and highly fragmented with low entry barriers [9][11]. **The whole year's working capital is consumed in the 3-4 month harvest window, and the risk is inventory, not the plant.** Capex is modest — a gin and press line — so most of our exposure will be stock and receivables. Peer AB Cotspin shows the trap: Q1 FY27 revenue up 52.94% to Rs 102.01 crore while operating margin fell to 12.90% from 22.29% [4][5]. **So when a proposal lands, check whether growth is coming from thinner spreads; if margins are falling while volumes rise, ask for the lot-wise purchase and sale register.**

## What has changed now
Gujarat GST collections are up 11.9% Apr-to-date against India's 6.1% [D], and IIP for NIC 13 (textiles) is up 13.1% YoY with output up 11.9% Apr-to-date [D]. **Bank credit is growing 15.2% against output of 11.9% [D] — money is chasing this trade faster than it is producing, so pricing discipline at the borrower level matters more than demand.** Downstream is healthy: Sportking nearly doubled EBITDA margin to 19.8% in Q2 FY27 from 10.4% [7], and Nitin Spinners expects its capex to add Rs 200-300 crore of revenue in FY2027 [6]. **Pursue ginners with direct supply relationships to such mills; avoid pure commission pressers and traders with no stock title.**

## How to grow safely
Structure as a cash credit against pledged stock with a drawing power computed on lint at the lower of cost or APMC-derived value, plus a bill-discounting sub-limit for mill receivables. **Take the stock statement and lot-wise kapas purchase register every month, and the APMC arrival and price sheet weekly during the harvest season.** Covenant a minimum margin of collect from customer and a maximum inventory holding period; if holding crosses the season, ask why the lot is unsold. Insist on a charge on the gin and press assets even where the ask is working capital only. ## Early-warning signs
- **Stock ageing beyond the season (monthly):** any lot held past the harvest window -> freeze fresh drawing and inspect the godown. - **Margin compression with volume growth (quarterly):** operating margin falling while revenue rises, as in the peer [4] -> reprice or reduce limit. - **Receivable days from spinning mills (monthly):** rising beyond agreed terms -> shift sales to bill-discounting against accepted bills only. - **Reliance on external borrowings for working capital (quarterly):** stretched capital structure [11] -> cap total bank exposure and demand promoter infusion. - **Client concentration (annual):** dependence on one or two mills -> require diversification before enhancement.
